title: Roos completeness, actual open completion units and the complete adjunction
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $e:V\hookrightarrow W$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Put $C_W(H)=R\lim Q_W(H)_\bullet$ and let $\eta_H:H\to C_W(H)$ be the actual strict quotient-augmentation map. Define $C_V$ likewise. Then $V,W$ are Noetherian and qcqs, $e$ is quasi-compact, and $(R,(t))$ satisfies the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $R$ is Noetherian, $A_1$ is additive torsion, every $A_n$ is finite and has the finite free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$. The open coefficient identifications $e^{-1}(A_n)_W=(A_n)_V$ and $e^{-1}B_W=B_V$ preserve constant sections and every quotient projection.
For every $H$, $C_W(H)$ is intrinsically derived $(t)$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and for every intrinsically complete $L$, precomposition with $\eta_H$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C_W(H),L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,L)$. The Roos-triangle completeness predicate [def-weil-derived-complete] holds for $H$ if and only if $\eta_H$ is invertible, equivalently if and only if $H$ is intrinsically complete; the same assertions hold on $V$.
There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\rho_H:e^*C_W(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_V(e^*H)$, induced by the coefficient-compatible reduction-tower comparison and the normalized exact-product Roos comparison, satisfying $\rho_H\circ e^*\eta_H=\eta_{e^*H}$. Restriction preserves completeness and its comparison to completed open pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is this actual completion unit, hence is invertible on complete objects. Extension $e_!$ preserves completeness. The open adjunction restricts to the full complete subcategories, its unit $M\to e^*e_!M$ is the identity under the section-normalized slice identification, and $e_!$ on these subcategories is fully faithful.

proof.text: The valuation ring $R$ is a PID and a domain, with finite residue field, by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. Thus each ideal is finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] every $A_n$ is finite. The additive group of $A_1$ is torsion because it is finite. Since $t\ne0$, multiplication by $t^n$ on $R$ is injective, its image is $(t^n)$, and its cokernel is $A_n$. Hence $0\to R\xrightarrow{t^n}R\to A_n\to0$ is a finite free resolution. This verifies every coefficient hypothesis of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], including perfectness, for $(R,(t))$.

source.place: Coefficient datum, using the two cited DVR results; the Noetherian and two-term resolution deductions are elementary.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $V,W$ are Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] gives quasi-separatedness, so both are qcqs. For each affine open $T\subset W$, the open subscheme $T\cap V$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. This is the affine-local definition that $e$ is quasi-compact.

Use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify the site of $V$ with the slice over the open. Its constant-coefficient identification takes $a\in A_n$ to the same constant section. For the quotient $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, the two possible composites therefore agree on constant sections, hence agree as maps of constant sheaves. The inverse-image functor preserves limits and is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation]. Apply it to $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ to obtain $e^{-1}B_W=B_V$; the induced comparison is characterized by the equalities of all quotient projections. These are the coefficient identifications claimed. Countable products are exact for both completed ring sheaves by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact].

source.place: Open localization and immersion limit preservation; coefficient identifications by the universal property of the limit. Countable-product exactness is the cited pro-etale product result.

proof.text: For $T=W$ or $V$, let $\Lambda_T(H)$ be the Koszul completion on $B_T$ for the global section $t$. The ringed Koszul reflector [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] says that $\Lambda_T(H)$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete and that its unit induces $\operatorname{Hom}(\Lambda_T(H),L)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(H,L)$ for every locally complete $L$. The intrinsic product-fibre construction and this strict derived-limit Koszul construction agree, including their units: [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies the product-fibre unit $(u_H,0)$ with the strict augmentation unit. By [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence], intrinsic completeness is precisely the local completeness condition in the reflector theorem. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-completed-koszul-quotient-comparison] supplies a natural isomorphism $a_H:\Lambda_T(H)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T(H)$ satisfying $a_H\kappa_H=\eta_H$. Therefore $C_T(H)$ is intrinsically complete. The bijection for $C_T(H)$ is explicitly $f\mapsto f\eta_H$: composing first with $a_H$ and then with $\kappa_H$ gives exactly this map. The same equivalence lemma identifies the Roos predicate, intrinsic completeness and invertibility of this specified $\eta_H$. This proves all reflector and predicate assertions on both sites.

source.place: Tags 099B, lemma-derived-completion, and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; proetale.tex Tag 099M. Completed-ring and actual-unit bridges are the cited nodes.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to H$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $e^*P$ is flat-term K-flat. On a slice object $T\to V$, restriction of $P\otimes_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ is canonically $(e^*P)\otimes_{B_V}(A_n)_V$: the tensor map sends $x\otimes a$ to the same tensor with its restricted coefficient, and its inverse is the same balanced tensor formula under the slice identifications. It commutes with $1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ and sends $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ to $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Thus these maps give a comparison $\tau_H:e^*Q_W(H)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_V(e^*H)_\bullet$ of strict tower complexes, including the augmentations. Naturality is already an equality on tensors. The derived pullback theorem and the functorial reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] make the resulting comparison independent of representatives.

source.place: Tags 0G7E, lemma-pullback-K-flat, and 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; strict slice tensor calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] to the exact product-preserving functor $e^*$ from Step 3 and its termwise action on strict towers. Define $\rho_H=R\lim(\tau_H)\circ\lambda_{Q_W(H)}$. This is a natural isomorphism $e^*C_W(H)\to C_V(e^*H)$. In normalized Roos coordinates $H_M^q=(\prod M_n)^q\oplus(\prod M_n)^{q-1}$, $\lambda=\theta^{-1}\kappa e^*\theta$ with $\kappa$ the canonical product comparison on both summands. In particular, the augmentation clause of the cited lemma and the strict augmentation equality of Step 5 give the equality $\rho_H\,e^*\eta_H=\eta_{e^*H}$. If $H$ is complete, $e^*\eta_H$ is invertible and hence so is $\eta_{e^*H}$; Step 4 proves completeness of $e^*H$. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], the comparison from ordinary to completed open pullback is induced by applying the tower pullback to the strict quotient augmentation. Step 5 identifies that augmented tower with the quotient tower of $e^*H$, so the comparison becomes exactly $\eta_{e^*H}$. It is therefore invertible on complete objects.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); normalized strict-limit augmentation comparison in the cited exact-product lemma.

proof.text: Exact extension by zero is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; it preserves countable products by [lem-cbc-ringed-open-extension-products], since Step 2 proves $e$ quasi-compact. For a flat-term K-flat $P\to M$ on $V$, [lem-sf-open-semilinear-tensor-model] says that $e_!P$ is flat-term K-flat and gives the simultaneous tensor isomorphisms $r_n:(e_!P)\otimes_{B_W}(A_n)_W\to e_!(P\otimes_{B_V}(A_n)_V)$ with formula $[x]\otimes a\mapsto[x\otimes a|_V]$. Forgetting the finite-ring actions yields an isomorphism $r:Q_W(e_!M)_\bullet\to e_!Q_V(M)_\bullet$ in strict $B_W$-module towers: extension by zero has the same underlying module sections before and after this scalar restriction. Its transitions and augmentations commute by the cited model. The strict-limit lemma now gives the natural isomorphism $\sigma_M=(R\lim r)^{-1}\lambda:e_!C_V(M)\to C_W(e_!M)$. Its augmentation clause gives $\sigma_M e_!\eta_M=\eta_{e_!M}$. Thus completeness of $M$ makes $\eta_{e_!M}$ invertible, and Step 4 proves completeness of $e_!M$.

source.place: Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; normalized strict-tower proof using open product preservation and the simultaneous open tensor model. Agent-written assembly.

proof.text: The specified exact open adjunction localizes termwise as in [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. By Steps 6 and 7 both functors preserve complete objects, and the complete subcategories are full, so its Hom bijections restrict unchanged to an adjunction between them. The open unit in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] is the identity on sections under the slice identification $e^*e_!M=M$. This remains the unit after restricting the Hom bijections. Explicitly, a map $e_!M\to e_!N$ corresponds under that bijection to a unique map $M\to e^*e_!N=N$; naturality of the unit says that the map corresponding to $e_!f$ is $f$. Hence $e_!$ induces a bijection on these Hom sets and is fully faithful on the complete subcategories.
